01Why Intellica

Training that ends with work you can show

Most courses end with a certificate of attendance. Ours end with a document, a design or a security pack for a system you know, built step by step and checked as you go.

You build something real

One growing artefact per course: an architecture file, a decision record, a security assurance pack. You finish with work you can show a colleague, an employer or a client.

Labs that guide you

Each lab step comes with a brief, a template, snippets, a model solution and a rubric, so you are never facing a blank page.

Honest about status

Every page says what is open, what is planned and what a certificate does and does not mean. We are not an accredited provider and we never imply it.

Evidence, with dates

Lessons cite their sources and show when they were last reviewed. Where research is thin or not about adult professionals, we say so.

Practitioner built

The courses come from the same work that goes into our agent, security and architecture systems, not from a textbook summary.

Yours to keep

One payment, lifetime access to your edition and its updates, a 7-day refund window and free preview lessons so you can try before you pay.

02Hands-on labs

Inside a lab

Every lesson is followed by a lab step. You write real work for your own system, never a throwaway exercise. Each step follows the same six moves, so you always know what to do next.

  1. 1. Read the briefWhat you are producing, why it matters and what done looks like.
  2. 2. Study the worked caseA finished example for a sample case, so you see the standard before you try.
  3. 3. Write your ownWork in the lab editor on your own system, starting from a template and snippets.
  4. 4. CompareOpen the model solution and see where yours differs and why.
  5. 5. Mark yourselfScore 0, 1 or 2 on four rubric criteria, then close the gaps you find.
  6. 6. Run the health checkA completeness check in your browser. Nothing is uploaded. Download the finished file at the end.

A health check confirms the work is complete and free of placeholders and secrets. It does not judge whether your design is right; the rubric and model solution do that, and you mark yourself. We say so on every course page.

03Technology

Tools you run, not slides you watch

Lab editor and health checks

Write in the browser, keep your progress on your device and run completeness checks locally. Your work is not sent to us.

Practice tools

Depending on the course: a scenario checker, a budget calculator, a policy tester and a trace spotter, all running in your browser.

Reference lab kit

The cyber security course includes a local lab (one Node file, no network, synthetic data) with seeded flaws to find and fix.

Mock exams

Level 1 includes three timed 40-question practice papers with a report by chapter and learning goal. They are original practice questions, not real exam questions.

Accessible lessons

Short slide lessons with a transcript for every slide, a read-aloud voice and recall questions that return for review.

Verifiable certificates

A credential ID and a public page that confirms completion under the published rule, shareable to LinkedIn or as a PDF.

04Process

How a course is made and kept current

  1. 1. ResearchWe read the primary sources: standards, curricula, papers and incident reports, and register each with its version and date.
  2. 2. DesignWe write outcomes first, then the lab that proves them, then the lessons that prepare you for it.
  3. 3. CheckAutomated checks test counts, links, claims and wording before anything is published, so pages cannot disagree with the courses.
  4. 4. Publish and dateEach lesson shows its review date and each course keeps a changelog.
  5. 5. UpdateUpdates to your edition are free. Where a curriculum changes, such as the 2027 iSAQB release, we refresh the mapping before it applies.

05Pedagogy

Every course follows the same loop

Study expert practice

The Architecture and Cyber Security Academies connect core concepts to worked examples and decisions drawn from real engineering and security work.

Build professional artefacts

Guided labs turn learning into architecture descriptions, security designs, test plans and other work products that can be reviewed and improved.

Retrieve, test and improve

Knowledge checks, practical tools, model solutions and rubrics help learners identify gaps and improve the quality of their work.

Learn from current evidence

The academies cite research and standards, record review dates and update their materials as evidence and technology change.

Research behind the method

  • Test-enhanced learningRoediger & Karpicke, Psychological Science (2006)

    Low-stakes recall questions help strengthen delayed retention; they are used to retrieve knowledge, not merely score it.

    Read the research
  • Distributed and interleaved practiceCepeda et al. (2006); Kirschner et al., Educational Psychology Review (2026)

    Spacing and interleaving support durable learning when practice and feedback elicit the right cognitive work. The 2026 meta-analysis covers school classrooms; its effect sizes should not be assumed for adult professional training.

    Read the research
  • Worked examples and scaffold fadingRenkl, Cognitive Science (2014 issue; first published 2013)

    Learners first inspect a complete worked solution, then complete partially supported tasks before independent performance.

    Read the research
  • Active learningFreeman et al., PNAS (2014)

    Applied tasks, explanation and decision-making supplement exposition; passive reading is not treated as evidence of competence.

    Read the research
  • Feedback and deliberate practiceHattie & Timperley (2007); Ericsson et al. (1993)

    Rubrics and model solutions make gaps visible; repeated practice is targeted at a specific weakness and followed by corrective feedback.

    Read the research
  • Deliberate practiceEricsson, Krampe & Tesch-Römer, Psychological Review (1993)

    Practice is targeted at a defined performance gap, repeated with informative feedback and adjusted as competence improves; seat time alone is not a measure of expertise.

    Read the research

Every course page identifies its current delivery status, the work it asks you to complete, how completion is recorded and how it relates to external qualifications. Available courses are distinguished from planned levels and assessments.

07Certificate

A certificate you can verify and share

After meeting the published course-completion criteria, learners can claim a certificate with its own credential ID and a public verification page. The certificate can be shared or saved as a PDF.

To earn it

  1. Finish every lesson
  2. Complete every lab step and pass its health checks
  3. Answer at least 70% of the check questions correctly, on the first try or in review

What you get

  • A credential ID and a public page that confirms it
  • Add to LinkedIn in one click
  • Share on LinkedIn, X or Facebook, or copy the link
  • Save as a PDF

The certificate records completion against the course rules, based on progress reported by the learner’s browser. It is self-reported and unproctored; lab work is not independently marked by Intellica. It is not accredited as a professional qualification and does not confer or replace an external certification.

08Before you enrol

Straight answers

Can I try before I pay?

Yes. Every open course has free preview lessons, and you can ask for a refund within 7 days of payment.

Is this an accredited qualification?

No. Completion certificates record that you met the published course rules. They are not iSAQB credentials, and no Intellica academy credential has been issued yet. Level 1 is independent self-study, not an iSAQB course.

How do I get access?

Pay by bank deposit from the course page, upload the receipt, and your access code opens the course. Keep the code private; it is personal.
